info.title: Tassyir developer API
info.summary: The API a developer calls to build Tassyir apps: their account, apps, client secrets, versions, the webhook console, dev stores and the CLI sign-in.
info.description:
The routes under `/developer/` that a DEVELOPER calls: the developer console, the `tassyir` CLI and the dev MCP. Not an app's API: installed apps call the Admin API (docs/api/apps/openapi.2026-10.json). Generated from the code by `npm run apps:openapi`; the reference is docs/api/apps/developer.md, developer-webhooks.md, dev-stores.md and developer-cli-auth.md.

**Authentication.** `Authorization: Bearer <dashboard JWT>` (the console) or `Authorization: Bearer tsy_dt_…` (a developer token from the CLI sign-in), on every route but the approval routes (the dashboard session only) and the two public RFC 8628 routes. A developer account belongs to a USER, not a business: no route takes a business id, and an id that is not yours answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist.

**Conventions.** JSON fields are camelCase (snake_case on the two OAuth routes, as RFC 8628 has them); ids are strings; times are ISO 8601 UTC. One resource answers `{ data }`, a paged list `{ data, nextCursor }` (pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`), a short list `{ data }`.

**Errors.** Not problem+json: the dashboard API's shape. A coded refusal is `{ statusCode, code, message, fix?, …subject, requestId }` (`DeveloperError`); act on `code`. Three refusals carry no `code` today: the ValidationPipe's 400 (`message` is a list of sentences), the dashboard session guard's 401, and the global rate limiter's 429 (a JSON string). The two OAuth routes answer `{ error, error_description }`. Each operation lists every code it can answer, by status.

**Limits.** Counted in the database per developer (apps, secrets, versions, dev stores) and in Redis for the console and the CLI sign-in, whatever the global rate limiter says; each operation says which apply.

Takes the dashboard session or a developer token (`tsy_dt_…`); either way the caller is the signed-in user, and only their own account, apps and tokens are reachable.

post.description:
A synthetic, signed delivery of a sample body (`tassyir-test: true`, `webhook-id: dlv_test_…`, envelope id `evt_0`); nothing is recorded and a 410 disables nothing. Needs an active installation whose version subscribes to the topic and was granted its scope. 20 tests per app and 40 per developer every 10 minutes.

post.summary: Upload a version of the app's manifest
post.description:
The body is at most 128 KB (8 MB + 128 KB while Tassyir Hosting is on) and nests at most 16 levels (its own parser). The validator checks the manifest (every error at once); `handle` must be the app's; a manifest identical to the latest version's (and, hosted, the same bundle) is refused. An external version is numbered latest + 1, approved and current at once. A hosted version (`hosting.mode = "tassyir"`, while Tassyir Hosting is on) carries its `bundle`, stored before the version is created `scanning`; it is scanned, uploaded and released by the hosting pipeline (docs/api/apps/developer.md "Hosted versions"). 30 uploads per developer per hour, 10 hosted a day.

Takes the dashboard session or a developer token (`tsy_dt_…`); either way the caller is the signed-in user, and only their own account, apps and tokens are reachable.

Reference: docs/api/apps/developer.md.

Print `user_code`, open `verification_uri_complete` (it only pre-fills the code: the developer approves on the page, signed in to the dashboard), then poll `POST /developer/cli/token` every `interval` seconds. 10 sign-ins per IP every 10 minutes. Errors are OAuth's `{ error, error_description }`.

Public: the CLI holds nothing yet.

Reference: docs/api/apps/developer-cli-auth.md.

post.description:
The approval page's route (dashboard JWT ONLY: a developer token can never approve a sign-in). The code travels in the body; dashes, spaces and case are ignored. An unknown, expired or someone else's code is one answer, 404 `CLI_CODE_NOT_FOUND`. 10 approvals per user an hour; 10 wrong codes per user and 30 per IP an hour. Only on the developer's click, never automatically. Idempotent. The CLI's next poll receives the token, and the developer is told (a bell notification and a push).

Takes the dashboard session ONLY: a developer token is refused here, so a stolen CLI token can never approve a new sign-in.

Reference: docs/api/apps/developer-cli-auth.md.

currentVersion.description: The number of the version new installations get; null before the first upload.

DeveloperAppList.description: Every app (at most 50) at once (not paged).

DeveloperError.description: A coded refusal of the developer API (the dashboard API's error shape, not problem+json). Act on `code`, never on `message`. Other members name the subject of the refusal (`appId`, `limit`, `retryAfterSeconds`, `status`, …).

code.description: Stable: what a client branches on.

fix.description: One sentence an AI agent can act on.

errors.description: With `APP_MANIFEST_INVALID`, `APP_FIELDS_INVALID`, `DEVELOPER_ACCOUNT_INVALID`: every problem at once, in the manifest validator's format.

path.description: With a body the parser refused: the request path.

requestId.description: Also in the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it to Tassyir.

id.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

businessId.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

appVersionId.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

version.description: The pinned version's number; null if it cannot be read.

state.description: `disabled`: nothing is sent (re-enable it); `failing`: deliveries fail since `failingSince` (disabled after 3 days of it).

DeveloperInstallation.description: An installation of your app, with its webhooks' health.

nextCursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` (with the same filters) for the next page; null on the last.

access_token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` to `developer/*` (nowhere else). Store it like a password.

expires_in.description: Seconds of idle expiry (90 days); every use extends it.

token_id.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

user_id.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

email.description: Who the CLI signed in as.

DeviceAuthorizationRequest.description: Form-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, parsed flat) or a flat JSON object: at most 8 KB and 20 parameters, every value one string of at most 4,096 characters, a parameter sent twice refused (`invalid_request`).

client_id.description: The client starting the sign-in; another is `invalid_client`.

client_version.description: Your version, shown on the approval page.

device_name.description: The machine's name, shown on the approval page and in the token list: letters and digits of any script, spaces and `._-'()@`, at most 64 characters after trimming.

device_code.description: Poll `POST /developer/cli/token` with it. Never show it.

verification_uri_complete.description: The same page with `?code=XXXX-XXXX`: it pre-fills the code, never approves.

DeviceTokenRequest.description: Form-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, parsed flat) or a flat JSON object: at most 8 KB and 20 parameters, every value one string of at most 4,096 characters, a parameter sent twice refused (`invalid_request`).

client_id.description: The client starting the sign-in; another is `invalid_client`.

FieldError.description: One problem, as the manifest validator reports it.

HttpError.description: A refusal without a `code`: the dashboard JWT's guard (no token, a revoked or expired session, a password changed since it was issued).

id.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

secretPrefix.description: `tsy_cs_` + the first 8 random characters: tells secrets apart, rebuilds nothing.

state.description: `active`: no end date; `expiring`: rotated out, valid until `expiresAt`; `expired` and `revoked` are refused by the token endpoint.

secret.description: Shown ONCE: Tassyir keeps only its hash. Lost means rotate.

rotated.description: The secrets this one rotated out: still live until their `expiresAt` (24 hours). Empty for the first secret.

IssuedSecretResponse.description: A minted client secret (served with `Cache-Control: no-store`).

OAuthError.description: An OAuth error (RFC 6749 §5.2, RFC 8628 §3.5), on the two public CLI routes only.

ServerError.description: An unexpected failure (500), or a database that cannot be reached (503: retry). Never an internal message: `requestId` names it.

ThrottlerError.description: The global rate limiter's refusal, a JSON string (`"ThrottlerException: Too Many Requests"`), only while rate limiting is enforced. A developer token's calls are counted by IP.

anyOf.description: An https URL with a public host name.

manifest.description: `tassyir.app.toml` exactly as a TOML parser returns it, handed to the manifest validator untouched (rules: docs/api/apps/manifest.md, schema: docs/api/apps/manifest.2026-10.schema.json). Anything else is 400 `APP_MANIFEST_INVALID`.

anyOf.description: A hosted version's code (required for `hosting.mode = "tassyir"`, refused otherwise): `{ main, files: [{ path, content }], lockfile? }`, text modules only, at most 100 files and 3 MB; checked by the bundle validator (every error at once, 400 `APP_BUNDLE_INVALID`). Rules: docs/api/apps/developer.md "Hosted versions".

ValidationError.description: The global ValidationPipe's refusal: a field missing, malformed or unknown, in the body or the query string. It carries NO `code`: branch on the status (400) and show `message`.

message.description: One sentence per refused field (`limit must not be greater than 100`).

id.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

installationId.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

businessId.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

errorClass.description: A coarse family of the attempt's error; null without one.

WebhookDelivery.description: One delivery of the log (metadata only: never a body or a URL).

nextCursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` (with the same filters) for the next page; null on the last.

reEnabled.description: False when the endpoint was not disabled.

WebhookEnableResponse.description: The installation after re-enabling its webhooks.

WebhookReplayResponse.description: The delivery after one more attempt, and what it came to.

webhookId.description: The `webhook-id` the test was sent with.

installationId.description: A Tassyir id: a string of digits.

status.description: `delivered` on a 2xx; a test is never retried.

errorClass.description: A coarse family of the attempt's error; null without one.

WebhookTestResult.description: What your endpoint answered to a test delivery.
